hello.note: The reply is Dia is Muire duit. To several people: Dia daoibh. Casually: haigh.

goodbye.note: If you are leaving, say slán agat; to someone who is leaving, slán leat.

please.note: To several people: le bhur dtoil.

thank_you.note: To several people: go raibh maith agaibh. Thanks a million: go raibh míle maith agat.

youre_welcome.note: Also very common: ná habair é (don't mention it) or níl a bhuíochas ort.

yes.note: Irish has no true word for yes; you echo the verb: An bhfuil tú réidh? – Tá. Sea is the general form.

no.note: Usually you echo the verb: An bhfuil tú réidh? – Níl. Ní hea is the general form.

sorry.note: For a small slip or bump, gabh mo leithscéal is also common.

excuse_me.note: Said roughly 'gow muh lesh-kayl'. To several people: gabhaigí mo leithscéal.

good_morning.note: Also: Dia duit ar maidin. Traditionally Dia duit serves at any time of day.

how_are_you.note: Connacht: Cén chaoi a bhfuil tú? Ulster: Cad é mar atá tú? Irish uses tú for everyone.

im_fine.text: Tá mé go maith, go raibh maith agat
im_fine.note: In Munster: Táim go maith. Also: go breá (fine) or ar fheabhas (great).

whats_your_name.note: Connacht: Cén t-ainm atá ort? Ulster: Cad é an t-ainm atá ort?

my_name_is.note: The name comes first: Seán is ainm dom. Also common: Is mise Seán.

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also common: is deas bualadh leat. In Connacht: castáil leat instead of bualadh leat.

where_from.note: Also heard: Cé as thú? (Connacht), Cad as duit? (Munster).

im_from.note: E.g. Is as Éirinn mé. Countries with 'an' change: Is as an bhFrainc mé (France).

speak_english.note: Irish says you 'have' a language. Also heard: An labhraíonn tú Béarla?

dont_understand.note: Said roughly 'nee hig-im'. Ní thuigim thú = I don't understand you.

speak_slowly.text: Labhair níos moille, le do thoil
speak_slowly.note: To several people: labhraígí níos moille. Softer: An bhféadfá labhairt níos moille?

where.note: Before a verb it is just cá: Cá bhfuil sé? (Where is it?)

what.note: Connacht: Céard? Ulster: Cad é? To mean 'pardon?', say gabh mo leithscéal?

who.note: Usually with more: Cé hé sin? (who's that – a man), Cé hí sin? (a woman).

how_much.note: Ulster: Cá mhéad atá air seo?

where_bathroom.text: Cá bhfuil an leithreas, le do thoil?
where_bathroom.note: On toilet doors: Fir = men, Mná = women.

can_you_help.note: More polite: An bhféadfá cabhrú liom? Ulster uses cuidiú for cabhrú.

what_time.note: Answer: Tá sé a trí a chlog (It's three o'clock).

what_means.note: Also: Cad a chiallaíonn sé seo? For a word: Cad is brí leis an bhfocal seo?

one.note: Counting form. With a noun: noun + amháin, e.g. cupán amháin (one cup).

two.note: With a noun: dhá, e.g. dhá chupán (two cups).

three.note: Counting people uses special forms: beirt (two people), triúr (three people).

four.note: With a noun: ceithre, e.g. ceithre chupán (four cups).

six.note: Said 'shay': s before e or i sounds like 'sh'.

seven.note: Said roughly 'shakht'. With a noun: seacht gcupán (seven cups).

eight.note: The h is only for counting; with a noun: ocht gcupán (eight cups).

ten.note: With a noun: deich gcupán (ten cups).

water.note: Said 'ish-ka'. Whiskey comes from uisce beatha, 'water of life'.

tea.note: Said 'tay'. A cup of tea: cupán tae.

im_hungry.note: Literally 'hunger is on me': many feelings are 'on' you in Irish.

bill_please.note: Also: an cuntas, le do thoil.

no_meat.note: I'm a vegetarian: is feoilséantóir mé.

enjoy_meal.note: To several people: bainigí taitneamh as bhur mbéile!

left.note: Turn left: cas ar chlé. Also written ar clé.

right.note: Turn right: cas ar dheis. On your right: ar do dheis.

straight_ahead.note: Also: díreach romhat (straight in front of you).

stop_here.note: Also: stad anseo, le do thoil.

want_to_go.note: Before 'the', use go dtí: Ba mhaith liom dul go dtí an t-aerfort.

is_it_far.text: An bhfuil sé i bhfad ó seo?
is_it_far.note: Answers: tá (it is) or níl (it isn't).

too_expensive.note: Ró- means 'too', as in rómhór (too big).

cheaper.text: An bhfuil aon rud níos saoire agat?

id_like_this.text: Ba mhaith liom é seo, le do thoil

just_looking.text: Níl mé ach ag féachaint thart
just_looking.note: Connacht: ag breathnú thart; Ulster: ag amharc thart.

pay_card.text: An féidir liom íoc le cárta?

cash.note: Literally 'dry money'. Paying in cash: ag íoc le hairgead tirim.

later.note: In speech also: ar ball (in a while).

good_evening.note: Many speakers simply say Dia duit at any hour.

see_you_later.note: Also: slán go fóill (bye for now).

wait_moment.note: To several people: fanaigí nóiméad. Also: fan go fóill.

call_police.note: In Ireland the police are the Gardaí; elsewhere say na póilíní.

need_doctor.note: Also: teastaíonn dochtúir uaim. Ulster: tá dochtúir de dhíth orm.

dont_feel_well.note: Simpler: níl mé go maith. I'm sick: tá mé tinn.

lost_phone.note: Also: chaill mé mo ghuthán (the Ulster word).

allergic.note: E.g. Tá ailléirge orm le cnónna (nuts).

be_careful.note: Watch out!: Seachain! To several people: bígí cúramach!

i_like_it.note: For a feminine noun: is maith liom í.

dont_like_it.note: For a feminine noun: ní maith liom í.

welcome.note: The famous warm version: Céad míle fáilte! To several guests: fáilte romhaibh!
